page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance in specific tasks, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier status at 36.49 GB/sec and 17.21 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations show limitations, with stress-ng multi-core performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rated as weak. Memory performance is mixed; while large block read-only bandwidth is average at 64.7 GB/sec, write bandwidth and small block cached read bandwidth are weak. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both perform at average levels, with Redis achieving 6.48 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.large offers a modern ARMv9 architecture with dedicated cores at a low resource density, making it a viable entry point for ARM-targeted development. The absence of local storage and the 1 Gbps baseline network speed represent clear tradeoffs for data-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for single-threaded utility tasks, lightweight web serving, Redis caching, and basic CI/CD pipeline tasks that do not require high multi-core scaling or large memory footprints.
